body: We had a [great discussion](https://github.com/openui/open-ui/issues/1133#issuecomment-2672751043) of the keyboard behavior today at OpenUI, and I'll be incorporating the conclusions into the explainer shortly. FYI. Thoughts appreciated, here or on the [OpenUI issue](https://github.com/openui/open-ui/issues/1133).

> We had a [great discussion](https://github.com/openui/open-ui/issues/1133#issuecomment-2672751043) of the keyboard behavior today at OpenUI, and I'll be incorporating the conclusions into the explainer shortly. FYI. Thoughts appreciated, here or on the [OpenUI issue](https://github.com/openui/open-ui/issues/1133).

I forgot to update this issue, but the explainer has been [updated](https://open-ui.org/components/interest-invokers.explainer/#keyboard) to incorporate the last OpenUI design session. The new behavior is that keyboard focus (after a delay) triggers the popover, but in a "not keyboard focusable" state. That keeps the popover from "stealing" the focus navigation order, if the user accidentally triggered it. Additional things will fully-activate the popover from that point. That requires a new `interactivity:not-keyboard-focusable` mode, and some new pseudo classes such as `:has-partial-interest`.

Thoughts appreciated.

I wanted to come back to this issue and discuss the "partial interest" concept. I've heard feedback from several folks (some a11y experts among them) that perhaps the partial interest concept is too heavy-handed, and not worth the potential benefit. Indeed, in the discussion above, I see these comments:

```
emilio: i wonder if showing accidentally the hovercard is such a big deal. ideally these would close with escape. if you tab on something you dont want to see, then you can press escape and its gone. seems like a simpler model to me
emilio: that would be my initial model
astearns: i also wanted to ask the same question, escape is not a new thing people have to learn. not a big fan of adding another magic key that you have to learn or have to get announced from the hovercard if its cluttering the ui there
astearns: i expect designers will have that help text be the first thing on the chopping block
```

I also have a concern that the feature might actually make it *harder* for keyboard users to understand what's going on, since they now have to press something special to get to the target popover's content, vs. just pressing the "normal" tab key to get there.

The partial interest concept adds significant complexity:
- The [pseudo classes](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/12154#issuecomment-2963548646) need to have a value for `partial`.
- There will need to be a pseudo element on the target popover that shows the "hint" text (e.g. "Press Alt-Up to activate"), so that it can be styled (or removed) by the developer.
- Implementation-wise, figuring out if partial interest is needed takes a bit of machinery, since the target popover needs to first be shown before its contents can be evaluated for focusability.
- Developers will have to contend with all of this, and I can see a desire to simply override it all and make there be just two states: no interest and full interest.

Given the above, it seems like this concept might be **a)** annoying to users, and **b)** annoying to developers. In which case, perhaps we should just remove this functionality? My anecdotal experience is that most hover-triggered popovers in the wild would not be seen as intrusive to users, since they contain at most one or two focusable elements (e.g. a "Follow" button), if they have any focusable content at all.

If in practice we find that such a feature is needed later, it seems like it could be added in a backwards-compatible way. Or at least the current [shape](https://open-ui.org/components/interest-invokers.explainer/#keyboard) of the proposal doesn't seem too breaking, if added later.
